headline: DBS CEO says repricing of AI financing risk is healthy
body: DBS CEO Tan Su Shan said investors are demanding higher returns and examining financing structures more closely, and she described the repricing as healthy. DBS has originated approximately S$25 billion in AI-related financing deals so far this year. Most of it supports hardware infrastructure, including semiconductors, memory chips and data centres.
note: For lenders, the practical point is her warning that financially weaker companies could face credit rating downgrades as markets reassess their AI exposure.

figure.label: AI-related financing DBS has originated so far this year, per its CEO

evidence.text: Speaking to Bloomberg Television on 12 October, Tan said investors are demanding higher returns and examining financing structures more closely.
However, Tan described the repricing as healthy, as investors seek to ensure that large financial commitments remain sustainable.
DBS has originated approximately S$25 billion in AI-related financing deals so far this year, according to Tan.
Most of the financing supports hardware infrastructure, including semiconductors, memory chips and data centres.
She warned that financially weaker companies could face credit rating downgrades as markets reassess their exposure to AI-related investments.
